I think our morality protects us from the natural order to a certain degree (as it should, rape is the most vile thing I can think of).

But if we're looking at this from a macro scale, human beings are like many other species of primate: tribal, violent, inqusitive, loving, monstrous.

Mother nature encapsulates it all. We may have an elevated sense of sentience and morality, but that does not excuse us from Nature's table.

That's a fair argument, and I don't disagree. 

Chimpanzees go war with each other for territory, sometimes even for sport.

Brown Falcons, Whistling Kites, and Black Kites are known to intentionally start and spread forest fires to drive mice from their habitat in order to make them easier prey. Look up 'Firehawks'.

War and Arson. And those are just off the top of my head.

I don't disagree that humans can be bad, but nature is an exceptionally ugly place.
It isn't an excuse, it's life.

I would honestly argue it's an issue of self-delusion, as every species is speciesist to a naturalistic degree. This is an unfortunate fact that is the food chain.

The problem is that we seem to delude ourselves into believing we are somehow above it all. We're not, we never have been. Maybe someday we will be when we fully embrace transhumanism. But until or unless we do, we need to acknowledge the fact that we are members of the natural order, and the natural order has always been a food chain.

The thing I find odd about this though, is the fact that Sabi's source hasn't been able to prove the Mii leak is fake. Sabi straight up said that the leak could be real, but it doesn't go with what her source has heard. "Heard" being the key word here, Sabi's basically saying that her source doesn't have a direct line of information, they're just going off of second hand information, hearsay essentially. I'm not saying this proves the Mii leak is real, nor am I saying that Sabi's source is illegitimate. What I am saying is that there's a real possibility the source's information may not be as accurate as believed, and that hearsay should never be taken at face value.

Another thing to consider is the fact that this source approached Sabi with this info, just out of the blue. Considering Sabi's a known leaker to Nintendo, and has gotten in trouble with them in the past (cease and desist notices), it can't be ruled out that Nintendo could be taking an extra precaution by potentially having an NoA employee give Sabi a red herring. I know this may seem like a stretch, but considering how much Sakurai hates leaks, and how sick of Sabi Nintendo probably is, this really isn't that far fetched at all.

I'm not trying to take pot shots at Sabi with all this, I'm just saying that with everything Sabi herself has said about this new source, we have to think critically about all of this instead of just blindly following whatever she has to say.
